title: Mistakes pardoned
hookLine: Allah has pardoned my community mistakes, forgetting, and what they're forced into
tomorrow: what if you lived like you were only passing through?

cards: Two in the morning, and the replay starts. The text sent to the wrong person. The name you forgot mid-introduction.
The number you got wrong in front of everyone. You didn't mean any of it, and it still plays on a loop. Yesterday's question: what if it's already pardoned?
Hadith thirty-nine, reported by Ibn Abbas and recorded by Ibn Majah: Allah has pardoned my community for mistakes, for forgetting, and for what they are forced into.

teach.b: Three things, each with a name. Khata': a mistake, missing the mark you were aiming for. Nisyan: forgetting.
And what you're forced into against your will.
What they share: none of them was chosen. The hadith isn't about a wrong you picked on purpose; that one has its own door, turning back to Allah. This one is about the misses.

teach.h: CONDEMN US NOT IF WE FORGET.
teach.b: The Qur'an ends its second chapter with a plea, in Pickthall's words: "Our Lord! Condemn us not if we forget, or miss the mark!" And Sahih Muslim reports that when it came, Allah answered: I have done so.
Here's the detail to tell a friend tonight.

teach.h: ALLAH FED HIM AND GAVE HIM DRINK.
teach.b: If someone fasting eats or drinks because they forgot, the Prophet, peace be upon him, said the fast stands: Allah fed him and gave him drink. The forgotten bite becomes a gift, not a failure.
One honest limit, as jurists explain it: the pardon is from sin, not from what's owed.
If a mistake broke your neighbor's window, you still fix the window. But the 2 a.m. weight, the one that says you're the mistake? This hadith sets that down.

how: Muslim jurists apply this hadith across the law: a fast broken by forgetting still stands, and acts done by honest mistake or under compulsion carry no sin, though damages owed to others are still repaid.

o: every wrong is wiped away, chosen or not
misses and slips carry no sin before Allah
only mistakes made at prayer are forgiven

p: Allah fed him and gave him drink

s: if a mistake is pardoned, you don't owe anyone anything for it
the pardon is from sin. if your mistake broke a window, you still fix the window.
someone fasting who eats because they forgot keeps the fast
the Prophet said: Allah fed him and gave him drink.
this hadith also pardons wrongs you chose on purpose
it covers mistakes, forgetting and force. a chosen wrong has its own door: turning back to Allah.

games.q: you completely forgot your best friend's birthday. not on purpose. she's hurt. what fits hadith thirty-nine?
o: it was forgetting, so no sin; still say sorry and make it up to her.
forgetting is pardoned, so there's nothing to apologize for.
feel guilty for weeks; that shows how much you care.
games.why: forgetting carries no sin, so the 2 a.m. weight can go. but what's owed to a person, like an apology, is still worth giving.

practice: If there's water near you, take one sip and hold it a moment before you swallow: the coolness, the plain taste. Bring one real mistake to mind, a miss, not a choice.
For the sit, on each out-breath, let it be called what the hadith calls it: a mistake, pardoned.

wordCard.voice: Mistakes pardoned: the miss, the forgetting, and the forced, lifted off by Allah's pardon. What's owed to people is still owed; the weight of sin is not.

orig.note: Arabic: mistakes and forgetting. two of the three things the hadith says are pardoned.

carryVoice: Your line: mistakes are pardoned, so fix what you can and set the weight down. Go gently.

sources.ref: Sunan Ibn Majah 2045; al-Bayhaqi (Ibn Abbas: Allah has pardoned my community mistakes, forgetting, and what they are forced into)

sources.q: Our Lord! Condemn us not if we forget, or miss the mark!

sources.ref: Sahih Muslim 126 (Allah's answer to the end of al-Baqarah: I have done so)
Sahih al-Bukhari 1933 (whoever forgets while fasting and eats or drinks: Allah fed him and gave him drink)
